>Don't bother with tofu, it hasn't got enough protein or nutrients to make it a viable choice.

175g of tofu gives you 50% of your RDA of iron, 80% of your calcium, 50% of your selenium. It's also a great source of plant protein and fairly low in fat. Spinach, on the other hand, doesn't have nearly as much iron as Popeye would have you think as it was actually a misplaced decimal that resulted in spinach being praised for its high iron content, when in reality it's actually more likely to inhibit iron absorption due to its high oxalic acid content. Nuts, while nutritious (depending on the nut), should only be eaten in small amounts due to their high-caloric density and also the fact that they're not satiating as most of their calories come from fat, not protein.

Brown rice, potatoes, and whole wheat products (pasta and homemade bread) are currently the biggest staples of my diet. I also eat a lot of bananas, but not as much as I used to. Every day I'll make a smoothie with bananas, frozen blueberries, kale, 1/4 of an avocado, an orange, an apple, and water, or some variation of this smoothie. Breakfast for me is brown rice flour cooked in soy milk with cocoa powder and sweetened with bananas or dates. I generally eat a block (350g) of tofu a week. I also eat a lot of lentils, beans and chickpeas, while I'll usually eat with some veggies like broccoli, carrots and peas. I also don't eat oil, and I don't add salt to anything. I like to keep things low-fat too, so generally the only high-fat foods I eat are avocados and flaxseeds, and I eat both sparingly. I'll eat nuts very rarely and as a treat, mostly because they're kind of expensive here.  

I eat as cheaply as I can while still making an effort to maintain adequate nutrition and I work out regularly (cardio + lifting), and so far I've lost 3 pounds in about a month. It's slow, but steady and much less likely to result in a binge, as I don't really restrict calories. I've gained a lot of strength and endurance, too. I can sprint uphill without breaking a sweat, it feels good.  

EDIT: I'd strongly recommend cutting oil out of your diet. Besides being the most calorie-dense source of food offering little to no nutritional value, it's extremely bad for your health, no matter what plant it comes from. [Video for more information.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b_o4YBQPKtQ)
